findings.description: Gate pipeline diagram routes a taken ADR number to "Rejected: re-steered; blocked after 2", but decision 146 makes it a refusal: no rejection counted, nothing steered.
findings.body:
The pipeline diagram sends `adr -->|taken| rej`, and `rej` is *"Rejected: report re-steered into the session; blocked after 2"*, which loops back to running.

Decision 146 says the opposite ([ADR 146 L58-60](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d1f9d5d06e068644ca612420d4f1cd2a1ef392/docs/adr/0146-the-gate-refuses-an-adr-number-the-target-or.md#L58-L60)): *"A refusal, not a rejection. … it consumes no rejection: the gate records it as `refused` (`refuseGate`), the session keeps its state and its reject count, and nothing is steered."* The source agrees ([merge-gate.service.ts L2925-2929](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d1f9d5d06e068644ca612420d4f1cd2a1ef392/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2925-L2929)). An ADR-number failure goes to `refuseGate`, not `failed()`.

This matters because a reader who hits a duplicate ADR number will wait for the worker to be re-steered. In fact nothing steers it, so they have to renumber the ADR or steer the session themselves. The page's own prose (around L33-35) says the clash "refuses the merge", so the diagram also contradicts the text.

The soft-flag edge (`soft -->|yes, no --accept-debt| rej`, L25) has the same problem. It also goes through `refuseGate` ([L2374](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d1f9d5d06e068644ca612420d4f1cd2a1ef392/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2367-L2374)).

The fix: point both edges at a separate `refused` node (recorded, nothing merged, no rejection counted, nothing steered).

findings.description: Guide says `pup launch` and `pup kill` refuse everyone but the operator; the source lets the conductor launch and plain-kill, refusing it only `kill --respawn`.
findings.body:
concepts.md L45-46 defines the operator, then says *"Some commands refuse everyone else: `pup launch` and `pup kill` ([42])"*. commands.md L53 also marks `pup kill <session> [--respawn]` as *(operator)*.

The source and the later decision say otherwise:
- `pup launch` refuses only a calling **session**: *"Admitting work belongs to the operator and the conductor"* ([index.ts L1416-1422](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d1f9d5d06e068644ca612420d4f1cd2a1ef392/src/cli/index.ts#L1416-L1422)).
- `pup kill` refuses the conductor only for `--respawn`: *"The plain kill is the conductor's; the hard respawn is not."* ([index.ts L2296-2311](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d1f9d5d06e068644ca612420d4f1cd2a1ef392/src/cli/index.ts#L2296-L2311)).
- [ADR 47](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/d1d1f9d5d06e068644ca612420d4f1cd2a1ef392/docs/adr/0047-a-conductor-session-is-the-operator-s-delegate.md) widened ADR 42's tier so the conductor can plan, create, launch and kill.

The guide also contradicts itself. commands.md L35 marks `pup launch` as *(operator or conductor)*, and concepts.md L43 says the conductor holds every operator power except the merge.

This matters because a reader would think the conductor cannot launch or kill workers, and would step in by hand for no reason.

The fix: in concepts.md, say that worker sessions cannot run `pup launch` and `pup kill`, and cite ADR 47 with ADR 42. In commands.md L53, say a plain kill is operator or conductor and `--respawn` is operator only.

findings.description: The `pup new` row has no operator/conductor marker, though `pup new` refuses worker sessions (src/cli/index.ts L1262); mark who may run it, as other rows do.

The lifecycle diagram shows `merged --> running: pup fix` but leaves out the return edge. A `pup kill` on a fixing session sends it back to `merged`, not `killed` (session-state.utils.ts L39-45), so the PR stays landable.

refuted_findings.description: Mermaid node labels contain an unquoted `;`, which mermaid parses as a statement separator, so the pipeline diagram may fail to render.
refuted_findings.refutation: In mermaid's flowchart grammar, `[` and `{` enter a text lexer state whose TEXT token excludes only brackets, braces, parens, pipe and double quote. So `;` inside node text is plain label text, and SEMI is recognised only between statements. The `;` problem applies to sequence diagrams, not flowchart labels. This rests on grammar knowledge, since the validator could not render the diagram; a live-editor check would settle it.

process_issues.description: The docs reviewer ran out of budget before covering everything. It did not read best-practices.md, troubleshooting.md, docs/guide/README.md or the README.md diff. It checked only a sample of ADR links and some flag spellings (it did not check merge --approved-by or the land --accept-head/--remeasure/--abandon-closed flags). Those pages and flags went unreviewed for accuracy this round.

Spawned only docs and conventions because the PR changes markdown only. Skipped correctness, security, context, simplicity, guards and maintainability (no code changed), workflow-safety (no workflow change) and spec (no --spec and no closing issue; the PR body's acceptance list is not a spec source under the protocol).
